pages:
§5I§0 stoop down to pick up the camera. 

It’s light, and the surface feels surprisingly clean. 

Considering the state and nature of this place, there’s little doubt that this is no ordinary camera.

§5I§0 remove the lens

cover and hit the power button. 

It springs to life, the little screen almost blinding §5me§0 compared to the darkness §5I’ve§0 become acclimated to.

When the screen finally transitions to the actual view, it isn’t what §5I§0 expect.

Rather than seeing the pitch black below the stairs, or the barely visible light on the upper floor, the camera shows §5me§0 everything in white to black with every shade of gray between. 

An infrared camera. 

§5I§0 put §5my§0 own hand in

front of it. 

The background darkens hastily to adjust to the new, most violent heat source it can see; §5my§0 digits glow bright white on the camera’s LCD. 

§5I§0 am not any more confident in §5my§0 ability to face whatever the hell is down there, but

at least this has removed §5my§0 excuse that §5I§0 can’t see. 

No matter how much §5I§0 don’t want to face it, §5I§0 have to go down there. 

The camera pans to below the steps, §5my§0 new third eye revealing what sits below §5me§0.

The landing at the bottom of the steps is a  hallway that leads to the right, and the left opens into a large, empty space. 

The camera doesn’t show what, but there’s a shape on the wall that §5I’m§0 guessing is a picture frame. 

§5I§0 can barely tell what

§5I’m§0 looking at. 

The temperature seems fairly uniform, so only very faint outlines of the environment are actually visible.

Beyond the general shape of the hallway, the room, the walls, the steps, and the corner, §5I§0 can’t see

any finer details. 

Nothing grants §5me§0 the excuse to run and hide. 

§5I§0 need to know where the hell §5I§0 am, and §5I§0 need to find a way out. 

§5I§0 trek down the stairs, one step at a time. A revolting

sensation of disgust strikes §5my§0 soul as §5I§0 set foot on the second to last step, and meet the sound of squishing. 

The carpet on these steps is utterly soaked. 

What the fuck? Why is this flooring so wet?

Has this place been flooded or something?

§5I§0 can’t see how that would be possible, given the…

circumstances 

of this place. 

The soggy carpet cares little for what §5I §0consider impossible.

No matter how hard §5I§0 try to not believe it, the carpet is wet. 

The last two steps are soaking wet. 

But the floor 
is not wet. 

No, that is a bit misleading. 

It would be more

accurate to say it isn’t just wet. 

It’s completely flooded. 

§5My§0 foot plunks as §5I§0 step with the force that a floor would ask for, but §5I’m§0 met with the face of water.

Water that reaches at least a few inches,

into §5my§0 shoe and through §5my§0 sock. 

Fucking awesome. 

Flooding across the entire lower level of wherever this place is. 

At least 6 inches of water seems to cover the entire floor.

§5I§0 realize now that the air is extremely humid. 
§5I§0 am filled with a deep sense of dread. 

The air seems to carry a sickly sense of rot that would come with long standing stagnant water.

Whatever has happened here, it’s

been like this for a long time. 

This is fucking disgusting. 

§5I§0 turn the camera down to §5my§0 feet. 

It shows them abruptly disappearing in a dark gray wall that seems to ripple across its surface.

The ripples grow faint quickly, becoming nearly imperceivable after just a few feet, but the fact that they don't stop abruptly tells §5me§0 that this entire place is like this. 

Well, §5I’m§0 already one foot in. Might as well keep going. §5My§0 second foot makes a much

more polite thunk into the water, the waves barely even registering on §5my §0thermal camera. 

§5I§0 turn the camera up, and decide where to go. 

To the left, into what looks like a living room, or to the right, where §5I§0 see a few

doors on each side of the hallway. 

§5I§0 wade through the water into the big empty room. 

§5I§0 can only assume this is meant to be a living room, because the thermal camera shows nothing. 

The temperature is

too even to distinguish anything, but §5I§0 don’t see even an outline of furniture. 

Panning around and observing the walls, the floor, the way §5I§0 just came, it’s all a sheet of indistinguishable gray on the screen of the thermal camera.

This is pissing §5me§0 off now. 

§5My§0 previous anxiety is gone, replaced with frustration. 

There’s nothing here. 

Nothing fucking anywhere. Why is this place empty? What the hell is going on here?

Wait. What’s that?


In the corner opposite where §5I§0 entered, there’s a slightly glowing area in the water. 

Where everything is nearly the same type of gray, this spot is much brighter.

Warmer. 

The screen doesn’t display temperatures for some reason, just the difference between regions, but this is distinctly brighter than everything else. 

The anxiety comes back. §5I§0 awkwardly approach the hotspot

in the water, treading §5my§0 feet with care as to not splash the water. 

Standing over top it, §5I§0 reach down and into the water. 

Christ, the water is cold on §5my§0 fingers. 

It’s not that cold against §5my§0 feet, but

for some reason it’s freezing on §5my§0 hands. 
But what they meet in the water warms them. 

With the warmth it provides, it also grants texture. 

Texture that §5my§0 brain recognizes instantly. 

§5My§0 coat.
